jobs.title: Director, AI, Data & Analytics
jobs.description:
The City of North Vancouver is the urban core of the beautiful North Shore and has a long-term vision to be “The Healthiest Small City in the World”, with five key priorities to be a City for People, a Resilient City, a Vibrant City, a Connected City and a Prosperous City. The City of North Vancouver is committed to adopting AI deliberately: grounded in policy, guided by ethics, and accountable to open information principles. We are seeking a Director who is responsible for Artificial Intelligence (AI) governance, and who can deliver transformation from that foundation.

Reporting directly to the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), this innovative and strategic leadership role will directly shape how artificial intelligence, enterprise data, analytics, and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) transform municipal service delivery. The Director will develop and implement strategies that modernize service delivery, improve organizational performance, and strengthen the City's ability to make informed, data-driven decisions. This is a transformative role that merges business acumen, strategic insight, innovation, and technological expertise to realize the full potential of AI and Data beyond automation and productivity improvement. As the City's steward for the ethical use of AI and data, the Director will build the governance framework, policies, and safeguards that make that transformation trustworthy.

As Director, AI, Data & Analytics, you will provide enterprise leadership for the City’s AI, data, analytics, and GIS functions. Working closely with the CAO, Executive Leadership Team, departmental leaders, and Information Technology Services, you will build the governance, capability, and partnerships that turn strategy into better services for the community.

Key Responsibilities

In this role you will:
Lead the City's responsible AI governance: develop and maintain the AI governance framework, policies, and standards.
Develop and lead the City’s enterprise AI, Data & Analytics Strategy aligned with Council’s Strategic Plan and organizational priorities.
Provide strategic advice to the CAO and Executive Leadership Team on digital innovation, emerging technologies, and enterprise transformation.
Lead enterprise initiatives that improve service delivery, organizational performance, and data-driven decision-making.
Lead enterprise data analytics, business intelligence, and open data initiatives.
Provide strategic leadership for the City’s enterprise Geographic Information Systems (GIS) program and geospatial strategy.
Partner with Information Technology Services to ensure technology investments support business transformation and organizational priorities.
Build organizational capability through AI literacy, data literacy, change management, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Lead a multidisciplinary team while managing budgets, resources, strategic partnerships, and enterprise programs.

Qualifications

You are an accomplished leader who combines strategic leadership with strong business acumen and a passion for innovation, with:
Extensive (ten or more years) senior leadership business management experience leading enterprise transformation, innovation, technology, analytics, or digital modernization initiatives.
Five or more years of AI experience in information-intensive industries or digitally advanced enterprises.
Five or more years of progressive experience building collaborative, high-performing teams and fostering a culture of innovation and continuous learning.

Experience developing enterprise strategies and cross-organizational programs.
Demonstrated success leading complex organizational change across multiple business functions.
Strong knowledge of artificial intelligence, analytics, GIS, and emerging technologies.
A thorough understanding of responsible AI principles, privacy, security, ethics, and regulatory considerations.
Exceptional relationship-building, communication, and influencing skills with the ability to engage executives, elected officials, staff, and external partners.

Education

Preferably a master’s or Ph.D. in business administration, in statistics, economics, science, technology, engineering, and mathematics or applied mathematics (STEM); computer science; artificial intelligence; data science; information systems or related field; or equivalent work experience. Academic qualification or professional training and experience in legal and regulatory areas are also desirable.

Salary:
We offer an attractive remuneration and benefits package for this exempt position, including a compressed work schedule. The salary range is $156,156.00 to $181,632.00.

During the recruitment process, applicants will be requested to provide a current Police Information Check (PIC).

If you are passionate about making the City of North Vancouver an even greater place to live, work and play, apply on-line through the Career Portal at www.cnv.org by Friday, November 20, 2026.

We are committed to being an inclusive employer—one that reflects the diversity of our community and values the unique contributions of each person. Guided by our core values and Council’s vision for an open and inclusive city, we work to create respectful, safe, and accessible workplaces. We regularly review and improve our hiring practices to help identify and remove barriers. Through ongoing learning, we continue to address any that remain.

We welcome applications from all qualified candidates. If you need an accommodation during the selection process, or are having trouble completing or submitting your application, please contact us at hr@cnv.org
. We’re here to support your full participation.

jobs.title: Chief Information Officer
jobs.description:
At SaskTel, big ideas come to life. We're a team of curious thinkers, bold innovators, and problem-solvers who make technology work better for people, businesses, and communities across Saskatchewan. Bring your energy, share your ideas, and help us shape what's next.

Chief Information Officer

SaskTel is entering a defining period of change. As the organization accelerates its transformation into a modern tech-forward communications leader, we are seeking a Chief Information Officer (CIO) who can bring clarity, courage and conviction to a division that sits at the centre of SaskTel’s future. This is a role for a leader who thrives in complexity, sees opportunity in legacy, and understands how to evolve a technology function into a true strategic engine for the business.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the President & CEO, the CIO is accountable for SaskTel’s enterprise technology strategy, digital modernization, cybersecurity posture, data governance, and the delivery of reliable, secure, and efficient technology services. The CIO also serves as SaskTel’s Chief Security Officer and holds enterprise accountability for data governance. This leader will oversee a large, diverse team responsible for enterprise applications, infrastructure, cloud services, cybersecurity, architecture, and service delivery. This role requires a leader who can modernize a complex, legacy-heavy environment and ensure they have a high-performing team who is willing and welcoming of the new technology horizon SaskTel is entering into.

The Mandate

For SaskTel, the role goes beyond providing telecommunications services. Technology connects Saskatchewan, strengthen communities, enables businesses and support the province’s economic growth. As technology continues to reshape how we live and work, it is increasingly central to Saskatchewan’s future. This is not a caretaker role. It is a once-in-a-career mandate to modernize, simplify, and elevate a technology environment that underpins every connection SaskTel delivers.

The Ideal Candidate

As the ideal candidate, you are a seasoned technology executive with a proven record of leading large, complex organizations through meaningful modernization. You bring deep expertise in enterprise systems, cloud transformation, cybersecurity, and data governance, paired with the leadership presence and elevate information services as a true strategic partner.

You have assembled 15+ years of progressive technology leadership experience, including significant time at the senior-executive level, and a history of modernizing legacy environments, improving delivery performance, and driving cultural change. You understand how to strengthen execution, introduce modern development practices, and lead teams through ambiguity with clarity and confidence.

Academically grounded with a bachelor’s degree in a relevant field, such as business, technology, or a related discipline and you are comfortable operating in regulated or public-sector environments. Experience with large-scale enterprise transformations, including OSS/BSS, CRM, ERP, or cloud-native modernization, is highly valued.

Above all, you are courageous, collaborative, and forward-looking. You bring the courage to challenge entrenched norms, the backbone to make risk-based decisions, and the leadership maturity to reset a long-standing operating model. You build trust quickly, communicate with executive presence, and bring the mindset and energy required to help SaskTel evolve. If you are energized by meaningful transformation, if you thrive in environments where change is both necessary and possible, and if you want your work to matter beyond the balance sheet, this role offers a rare platform to make a lasting impact.

To Apply

For additional information or a confidential discussion, contact Leadership Source at 306-543-1666 or search@leadershipsource.ca
. Applications may be submitted confidentially through clicking here. Early applications are encouraged. The search may advance as strong candidates are identified.

At SaskTel, we believe in fostering a diverse and inclusive workforce that reflects the customers and communities we serve. We strive to create an environment where all employees feel empowered to contribute their unique perspectives, driving innovation and creativity, while advancing our efforts as Saskatchewan’s leading Information and Communications Technology provider

What makes SaskTel special is our people, and the fun, connected culture we create together. Our highly engaged employees bring diverse perspectives, collaborate across teams, and turn fresh thinking into meaningful results. Experienced leaders are there to listen, coach, and champion your growth, giving you opportunities to take on new challenges, build your skills, and move your career forward. Here, you can be yourself, feel supported, and do work you're proud of alongside people who celebrate ideas, achievements, and each other.

CULTURE AND VALUES

Upholds foundational values of honesty, integrity and respect.

Consistently demonstrates our culture: Think Big (Innovation and Courage), Make a Difference (Commitment and Community), Focus on Experiences (Simplicity and Agility), and working as OneSaskTel Team.

This is an on-site position located at the location(s) above. The successful candidate must be located within the province of Saskatchewan. Out of province/country candidates must be willing to relocate. Flexible work opportunities, in province, may be available.

At SaskTel, we believe in fostering a diverse and inclusive workforce that reflects the customers and communities we serve. We strive to create an environment where all employees feel empowered to contribute their unique perspectives, driving innovation and creativity, while advancing our efforts as Saskatchewan's leading Information and Communications Technology provider.

As one of Saskatchewan's Top Employers, we offer rewarding work, competitive salaries, comprehensive health and dental plans, pension plans, flexible work arrangements, paid time off, training & more! For more information on our benefits please click here: SaskTel's Benefits.

We value diversity as a key aspect of our culture. We are committed to providing equal opportunities for all candidates to participate fully in the recruitment process. If you need any accommodation at any stage of the process, please contact us confidentially at talent.acquisition@sasktel.com.

Do you currently work for Canadian Blood Services? All employees must apply via the internal career page.

Together, the work we do connects people and changes lives — including your own.

Be part of a dynamic, collaborative and caring organization committed to saving and improving lives. Thousands of patients depend on us every day for reliable access to safe blood, plasma, stem cells and organs and tissues.

About The Role

Canadian Blood Services is seeking a Regular Full-Time Associate Director, Portfolio Governance and Value Realization
to join our Enterprise Portfolio, Program and Project Management Office (ePMO)
team in our Ottawa or Toronto office.

The ePMO
team delivers programs and services that advance valuable organizational initiatives, ensuring they are completed on time and on budget. Our focus is on maximizing business outcomes for Canadian Blood Services and the people in Canada we serve.

As the Associate Director, Portfolio Governance and Value Realization, you will lead value realization and benefits tracking activities aligned with corporate strategy, corporate funding cycles, and the delivery of high-visibility projects and programs across the organization.

Reporting to the Director, Enterprise Program Enablement & Project Management Office, you will lead ePMO-led value realization activities across enterprise programs and provide guidance to support value-informed decision-making. You will contribute to enterprise portfolio management and reporting for all corporate priority projects, including ePMO projects; escalate issues requiring executive attention; and provide leadership to enterprise projects coordinated through process management. You will also ensure compliance with corporate portfolio reporting requirements and support the execution of select projects within the portfolio by fostering collaboration and integration across divisions. In addition, you will provide a challenge function across other ePMO activities, including reporting, automation and artificial intelligence (AI), data and analytics, and alignment with corporate strategy.

Formula for success

Leveraging your skills in ePMO operations, you will oversee value realization driven through programs, providing leadership, coordination, and management of enterprise PMO processes and functions.
Applying your expertise in value realization leadership, you will oversee the development of proposals and business cases, as required, to help articulate anticipated benefits and the value proposition.
Demonstrating your skills in influencing and negotiating, you will motivate and coach staff for high performance, act with transparency, and promote a problem-solving mindset and collaborative culture.
Utilizing your experience in benefits management and performance measurement, you will ensure all centrally delivered projects and programs have defined benefits, measured using key performance indicators, tracked, and communicated in a consistent and effective manner, and incorporate effective change and risk management controls.
Drawing on your skills in project interdependency management and prioritization, you will identify, manage, and address interdependencies between projects and prioritization to drive the greatest value.
Demonstrating your ability to lead with empathy and emotional intelligence, you will apply the advanced soft skills required to lead and motivate others to achieve deliverables, particularly when priorities and expectations may be in conflict.
Contributing your expertise in strategic initiatives and project leadership, you will take a lead role in developing and maintaining various initiatives and participate in special projects and corporate initiatives as assigned by the Director.
Applying your skills in performance improvement and governance, you will identify opportunities to improve performance and apply fit-for-purpose processes that balance governance and empowerment.
Fostering your strengths in people leadership and talent development, you will create a high-performing, engaged, and inclusive team environment by setting clear expectations, developing talent, supporting career growth and succession planning, and promoting continuous learning, collaboration, and professional development.
Applying your analytical and problem-solving skills, you will use your seasoned experience and knowledge to analyze highly complex problems, interpret business needs, and develop integrated, innovative solutions. This will often require deeper investigation of conflicting information and novel thinking to establish solutions.

Desired Education And Skills

A bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Commerce, Finance, Accounting, Engineering, Science, Public Administration, Health Administration, or a related discipline. A master’s degree (MBA, MPA, MSc, or equivalent) is considered an asset. An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience may be considered.
A minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience managing multiple projects and programs involving large teams, significant budgets, and multiple stakeholders, including at the executive level.
Demonstrated ability to build and lead teams, including managing, coaching, and developing project managers, employees, and contracted resources.
Proven ability to manage a significant project portfolio within a large organization, with a focus on value realization and measurable business outcomes.
Demonstrated success in establishing and maturing value-driven portfolios and programs that support organizational transformation and strategic objectives.
Expertise in process transformation and service delivery, including the ability to develop recommendations and present outcomes to executive leadership.
Strong analytical and technical capabilities, with the ability to leverage portfolio reporting, data analytics, performance metrics, automation, and artificial intelligence (AI) to improve decision-making, reporting, and operational efficiency.
Knowledge of corporate planning, budgeting, and financial management processes that support effective portfolio management and prioritization.
Familiarity with introducing new products or processes within a regulated environment is considered an asset.
Knowledge of managing and implementing process changes within a unionized workforce environment is considered an asset.
Demonstrated ability to develop and maintain project and portfolio documentation, reports, business cases, and executive-level presentations.
Familiarity with Agile methodologies and working within Agile teams is considered an asset.
Proficiency with relevant project and portfolio management tools, including Microsoft Project Professional and Microsoft Project Online (MSPO), is considered an asset.
Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills, including collaboration, facilitation, influencing, negotiation, and stakeholder engagement.
Strong financial and operational planning capabilities, with the ability to align resources, budgets, and priorities with organizational objectives.

What We Offer You

4 weeks’ vacation.
Comprehensive group health, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family.
Annual performance award of up to 10%.
Defined benefit pension plan.
Employee discounts, wellness programs, and access to professional development resources.

What You Can Expect

This role requires a minimum of 40% on-site presence at 1800 Alta Vista Drive, Ottawa, Ontario or 67 College Street, Toronto, Ontario. Additional on-site work may be required based on business needs. On-site expectations are subject to change and may be adjusted on a temporary or permanent basis.
You will work Monday to Friday, 37.5 hours per week, 7.5 hours per day.
Travel is required to attend meetings and to fulfill project commitments.

If this role resonates with you, we encourage you to apply by providing your up-to-date resume. This could be your first step towards a meaningful and inspiring career. Come to work each day knowing that you save lives.

We acknowledge that the work of Canadian Blood Services spans many Territories and Treaty areas across the country, and we are grateful for the Traditional Knowledge Keepers and Elders who have guided us in this important work. We recognize the land and waters that have inspired our work and offer gratitude to those Indigenous peoples on whose territory we work, live and play.

Diversity and inclusion play a vital role in ensuring health equity for patients across Canada. We are committed to reflecting Canada’s population in our organization and fostering an environment where all employees can be their authentic selves, with equal opportunities to succeed and contribute.

We thank all applicants for their interest. However, only those considered for an interview or those invited to participate in an assessment will be contacted. Emails are sent directly from our system, to ensure you receive them please add donotreply@blood.ca and system@successfactors.com to your safe senders list.

Applicants who require accommodation should discuss their needs with us.

jobs.title: Director, General Operations, Structured Finance
jobs.description:
You desire impactful work.

You’re
RGA ready

RGA is a purpose-driven organization working to solve today’s challenges through innovation and collaboration. A Fortune 200 Company and listed among its World’s Most Admired Companies , we’re the only global reinsurance company to focus primarily on life- and health-related solutions. Join our multinational team of intelligent, motivated, and collaborative people, and help us make financial protection accessible to all.

Coordinates cross functional project teams to develop financing solutions for RGA's regulatory entities. Leads and manages accounting and reporting functions on assigned structured finance transactions. Reviews and analyzes structured finance transaction information ensuring accuracy of data and design. Evaluates and recommends improvements to improve efficiency for internal financing processes.

Principle Duties

Manage a project team of professionals of varying levels (including investments, legal, and other corporate partners as needed) to structure and complete complex reinsurance transactions throughout the global organization. Provide a point of leadership as well as coordinate a collaborative effort to develop optimal solutions to meet legal entity and consolidated objectives.
Assist with coordinating the processes of analyzing transactions through interaction with the various technical experts in structured finance, accounting, legal, investments, tax, etc. Anticipate, identify, and resolve issues that arise during the RGA transaction analysis process to maximize the chance of a successful outcome. Work with the transaction team to identify any issues related to the transaction and coordinate with the appropriate technical experts to make sure these issues get properly resolved in a timely manner to maximize the chance of success. Note that this position does not need to have all the technical expertise to analyze a transaction and resolve every issue but must have enough of an understanding of the transaction, the issue, and the organization to coordinate an appropriate response to resolve issues and successfully complete a transaction.
Lead negotiations with external parties ensuring that RGA’s financing needs are met efficiently and lead the implementation of legal entity optimization strategies, such as restacking efforts.
Establish processes that ensure financing transactions and support processes are implemented and administered properly.
Work with business units to identify potential financing needs, including cash, collateral, and regulatory requirements, by currency. Provide technical subject matter expertise to design and propose solutions, including reinsurance structures, securities lending, structured asset designs, and other capital market motivated strategies to allow RGA to efficiently finance its regulatory requirements.
Assists with oversight and management of other team members and manages direct reports (if applicable) through activities designed to improve processes and the ability to respond to external and internal customer needs.
Performs month-end/quarterly/annual financial reporting functions as assigned, primarily those associated with Structured Finance financing transactions, including recording financial activity, creating various financial reports, analyzing data, preparing general ledger uploads, and reconciling various general ledger accounts, administration of assigned internal retrocession agreements, balance sheets and income statement accounts. This includes coordination with other departments or subsidiary management personnel to obtain and compile required data, reconciling, and recording financial results to general ledger, and analysis and compiling data based on a US GAAP and Statutory basis. May include preparation of quarterly and annual financial statements. Leads quarterly officer meetings for assigned subsidiaries
Supports the department’s internal control and audit compliance process. This includes, but is not limited to, maintaining the department’s internal control narratives and EUC and IPE/RR inventories, identifying and implementing improvements in processes and maintaining applicable sections of department procedure documentation, and leading the coordination of both internal and external audit requests.
Maintain regular and predictable attendance.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor’s Degree in Arts/Sciences (BA/BS) in business, with emphasis in accounting, finance or actuarial science or equivalent related work experience required
Master’s degree in Arts/Sciences (MA/MS) preferred

Work Experience

8+ Years of experience in accounting, auditing, or structured finance required
Financial modeling experience related to structured finance preferred
Actuarial experience preferred
3+ Years insurance/reinsurance accounting experience preferred

Skills & Abilities

Intermediate understanding of the US Life insurance and reinsurance markets required
Ability to quickly adapt to new methods, work under tight deadlines and stressful conditions required
Advanced level of listening, investigative, analytical, innovation and critical thinking skills; Advanced ability to translate business needs and problems into viable/accepted solutions required
Advanced ability to design and structure financing solutions, including reinsurance provisions, which meet RGA’s risk/return requirements as well as financing partner’s needs and regulatory requirements. This requires actuarial and accounting skills to address risk issues associated with proposed financing transactions. required
Highly advanced oral and written communication skills, demonstrating the ability to convey business terminology that is meaningful and well received required
Expert ability to balance detail with departmental goals/objectives required
Highly advanced skills in customer relationship management and change management required
Expert ability to manage multiple projects and/or teams simultaneously required
Expert ability to consult with individuals across a wide variety of operational, functional, and technical disciplines required
Highly advanced persuasion and negotiation skills when working with internal/external customers required
Highly advanced ability to make timely and effective decisions and produce results required
Ability to work flexible hours to accommodate international projects across multiple time-zones required

What you can expect from RGA

Gain valuable knowledge from and experience with diverse, caring colleagues around the world.
Enjoy a respectful, welcoming environment that fosters individuality and encourages pioneering thought.
Join the bright and creative minds of RGA, and experience vast, endless career potential.

We’re excited to get to know you and connect your unique skills with our global opportunities. To create a modern and seamless experience, we use artificial intelligence (AI) in parts of our preliminary screening process. This technology helps us personalize job recommendations, automate interview scheduling, evaluate candidates based solely on experience—without considering name, gender, or other personal details—and provide real-time answers through our chatbot. AI is used only during early screening and never makes hiring decisions. Your RGA recruiter will work closely with you every step of the way to ensure the process feels personal, thoughtful, and focused on you.

Compensation Range

$107,060.00 - $144,820.00 Annual

Base pay varies depending on job-related knowledge, skills, experience and market location. In addition, RGA provides an annual bonus plan that includes all roles and some positions are eligible for participation in our long-term equity incentive plan. RGA also maintains a full range of health, retirement, and other employee benefits.

RGA is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, color, age, gender identity or expression, sex, disability, veteran status, religion, national origin, or any other characteristic protected by applicable equal employment opportunity laws.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
Position Overview

The Director of Finance provides strategic leadership and overall direction for the finance department at Lopes Limited. As a key partner to the President, Vice-President and senior leadership team, the Director translates business priorities into financial plans, provides clear advice on financial performance and risk, and supports decisions that strengthen profitability, cash flow and long-term growth.
Reporting to the President, the Director is accountable for the quality, integrity and timeliness of financial reporting and for the effectiveness of accounting operations, financial controls and forecasting. The role leads and develops the finance team, establishes clear accountabilities and ensures financial information supports practical decisions across construction, fabrication and project operations.
The primary focus is Lopes Limited. When requested by ownership or senior leadership, the Director also provides financial guidance to sister companies, working with their management teams and finance personnel to strengthen planning, reporting and financial practices within the scope assigned.

What we offer as an employer

Competitive salary
Comprehensive benefits including dental, vision, disability, and life insurance
Company RRSP’s
Wellness and employee assistance programs
Opportunities to grow within your community
Company events
Work-life balance
Free Golf Membership
On-site medical clinic
On-site service center for vehicle repairs at discounted rates
A culture that is built on respect, health, safety, and integrity

Responsibilities

Strategic Financial Leadership:
Lead Lopes Limited’s financial strategy, advise senior leadership, evaluate investments and growth opportunities, and guide commercial decisions to strengthen profitability and financial resilience.
Forecasting and Performance:
Lead forecasting and financial reporting, while coaching department leaders to manage spend, understand results, and take corrective action
Financial Reporting and Project Profitability:
Manage financial closing, reporting, project & departmental costing, and external accountant coordination to ensure accurate financial statements, reliable performance analysis, and sound accounting practices.
Cash Flow Financing and Capital Planning:
Oversee cash flow, working capital, financing, banking relationships, including financial oversight of bonding, insurance and funding opportunities.
Financial Controls Compliance and Risk:
Direct financial policies, internal controls, risk management, tax compliance, secure records and intercompany accounting to ensure accurate reporting and financial accountability.
Finance Department Leadership:
Lead and develop the finance team, oversee accounting and payroll, support workforce and compensation planning, and improve financial systems, processes and coordination across departments.

Qualifications and Experience

Post-secondary education in accounting or business with a CPA designation or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Eight to ten years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including leadership of a finance team and responsibility for financial planning, reporting, and controls
Experience in construction, fabrication, industrial services, or other project-based business, with a strong understanding of job costing, work in progress, and revenue recognition.
Demonstrated ability to advise senior leadership, develop financial strategy, and translate complex information into clear recommendations.
Strong experience in forecasting and cash flow management.
Knowledge of Canadian accounting and tax requirements, with the judgement to engage specialized advisors when needed.
Experience managing relationships with external accountants, and other financial partners; exposure to multiple related companies is an asset.
Advanced Excel and financial systems skills, including the ability to improve reporting and use data to support decisions.
Proven people leadership, sound business judgement, and the ability to challenge assumptions respectfully while building productive working relationships.
High standards of integrity, accuracy, and confidentiality, with the ability to balance strategic priorities and operational deadlines.

We thank all candidates for their interest but only those considered for an interview will be contacted.

At Lopes Limited we are committed to being an equal opportunity employer. We offer a barrier free experience to applicants with accessibility needs. Requests for accommodation can be made at any stage during the recruitment process. Please contact us directly for such arrangements at jobs@lopes.ca

new_jobs.title: Director of Finance
new_jobs.description:
Position Overview

The Director of Finance provides strategic leadership and overall direction for the finance department at Lopes Limited. As a key partner to the President, Vice-President and senior leadership team, the Director translates business priorities into financial plans, provides clear advice on financial performance and risk, and supports decisions that strengthen profitability, cash flow and long-term growth.
Reporting to the President, the Director is accountable for the quality, integrity and timeliness of financial reporting and for the effectiveness of accounting operations, financial controls and forecasting. The role leads and develops the finance team, establishes clear accountabilities and ensures financial information supports practical decisions across construction, fabrication and project operations.
The primary focus is Lopes Limited. When requested by ownership or senior leadership, the Director also provides financial guidance to sister companies, working with their management teams and finance personnel to strengthen planning, reporting and financial practices within the scope assigned.

What we offer as an employer

Competitive salary
Comprehensive benefits including dental, vision, disability, and life insurance
Company RRSP’s
Wellness and employee assistance programs
Opportunities to grow within your community
Company events
Work-life balance
Free Golf Membership
On-site medical clinic
On-site service center for vehicle repairs at discounted rates
A culture that is built on respect, health, safety, and integrity

Responsibilities

Strategic Financial Leadership:
Lead Lopes Limited’s financial strategy, advise senior leadership, evaluate investments and growth opportunities, and guide commercial decisions to strengthen profitability and financial resilience.
Forecasting and Performance:
Lead forecasting and financial reporting, while coaching department leaders to manage spend, understand results, and take corrective action
Financial Reporting and Project Profitability:
Manage financial closing, reporting, project & departmental costing, and external accountant coordination to ensure accurate financial statements, reliable performance analysis, and sound accounting practices.
Cash Flow Financing and Capital Planning:
Oversee cash flow, working capital, financing, banking relationships, including financial oversight of bonding, insurance and funding opportunities.
Financial Controls Compliance and Risk:
Direct financial policies, internal controls, risk management, tax compliance, secure records and intercompany accounting to ensure accurate reporting and financial accountability.
Finance Department Leadership:
Lead and develop the finance team, oversee accounting and payroll, support workforce and compensation planning, and improve financial systems, processes and coordination across departments.

Qualifications and Experience

Post-secondary education in accounting or business with a CPA designation or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Eight to ten years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including leadership of a finance team and responsibility for financial planning, reporting, and controls
Experience in construction, fabrication, industrial services, or other project-based business, with a strong understanding of job costing, work in progress, and revenue recognition.
Demonstrated ability to advise senior leadership, develop financial strategy, and translate complex information into clear recommendations.
Strong experience in forecasting and cash flow management.
Knowledge of Canadian accounting and tax requirements, with the judgement to engage specialized advisors when needed.
Experience managing relationships with external accountants, and other financial partners; exposure to multiple related companies is an asset.
Advanced Excel and financial systems skills, including the ability to improve reporting and use data to support decisions.
Proven people leadership, sound business judgement, and the ability to challenge assumptions respectfully while building productive working relationships.
High standards of integrity, accuracy, and confidentiality, with the ability to balance strategic priorities and operational deadlines.

We thank all candidates for their interest but only those considered for an interview will be contacted.
